name: Samson
overview: Samson was a male judge of Israel from the tribe of Dan, uniquely known as the son of Manoah. He is famously noted for killing a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey, demonstrating extraordinary strength given by God. His role as a judge was marked by deliverance during a period of Philistine oppression.
namesAndTitles: The name Samson means "little one of Shemesh" or "strong," reflecting aspects of his character and divine empowerment. This proper name is recorded in Judges 13:24 and was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Samson is identified as the son of Manoah, as inferred from Judges 16:31. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for Samson apart from what is noted in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Samson stands out in the biblical narrative as a Nazirite judge empowered by God to deliver Israel from its enemies despite personal moral struggles. His incredible feats, including slaying a thousand men with a donkey’s jawbone, illustrate God’s strength working through imperfect individuals. His life exemplifies that divine calling and gifting are not contingent on human perfection, and even in failure, God’s purposes prevail.
